answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to mint a unique work relic: a time-stamped, non-replayable transcript of a hard task bound to one key. Peers treat that relic as the only admissible signal of personhood. Fresh keys begin at a trust nadir and remain there until independent attestors confirm the relic cannot be cheaply cloned. A key that reuses another agent's relic, or that forks after confirmation, is slashed back to the nadir and ignored for the rest of the epoch.
